appellations.name: Reims
appellations.summary: Reims is the historic capital of Champagne, where French kings were crowned in the cathedral, and the seat of many great houses: Veuve Clicquot, Ruinart, Taittinger, Pommery, Krug, Louis Roederer, Charles Heidsieck, Mumm, Lanson and Henriot. Their cellars run through Gallo-Roman chalk pits (crayères) under the Saint-Nicaise hill, part of the UNESCO listing of 2015. The commune itself has only a small vineyard.

Les Riceys is the largest wine commune of Champagne and the only one with three appellations: Champagne, Coteaux Champenois and the rare still Rosé des Riceys, made from Pinot Noir. appellations.name: Verzy
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
A grand cru on the north-eastern slopes of the Montagne de Reims next to the forest of the Faux de Verzy, whose twisted dwarf beeches are a natural curiosity. Verzy's Pinot Noir is firm and fresh, and it has more Chardonnay than most Montagne villages, giving lean, mineral wines.

It was one of the five villages promoted to grand cru in 1985. Most of its grapes go to the houses, but the village's growers bottle Verzy under its own name.
appellations.terroir: North-east-facing slopes of chalk under the forested plateau of the Montagne.
appellations.nerd_note: The Faux de Verzy are a rare population of dwarf, twisted beeches (and some oaks and chestnuts) with a genetic mutation; the forest is protected.

appellations.terroir: North-facing slopes of the Montagne de Reims, with chalk close to the surface on the steeper parts and sandier, clay-rich soils near the forest edge; the cool exposure gives fresh, firm fruit.
appellations.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier

In the Bar-sur-Aubois, the eastern half of the Côte des Bar, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone, the Jurassic rocks of Chablis rather than the chalk of the Marne; the wines are ripe and fruity. Drappier, whose cellars were built by Cistercian monks of Clairvaux in the twelfth century, is based here; Charles de Gaulle drank Drappier at his home in nearby Colombey-les-Deux-Églises.
appellations.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

appellations.name: Louvois
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, with some Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
A Pinot Noir grand cru at the southern edge of the Montagne de Reims, in a gap of the forest north of Bouzy. Its vineyard is small and partly enclosed by woods, which keeps it cooler than Bouzy, and its Pinot is fresh, firm and red-fruited.

The village is dominated by the château built in the seventeenth century for the Marquis de Louvois, Louis XIV's minister of war. Most of the grapes go to the houses, so village-named bottles are rare.
appellations.terroir: Chalk slopes at the foot of the Montagne's forest, cooler and later-ripening than Bouzy and Ambonnay.
appellations.nerd_note: The Marquis de Louvois, François-Michel Le Tellier, was Louis XIV's secretary of state for war.
appellations.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

On the right bank of the Marne the main slopes face south toward the river; Meunier is the leading grape on clay and marl over chalk, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on the best sites.

appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
The hilltop village of the Benedictine abbey of Saint-Pierre, where Dom Pierre Pérignon was cellarer from 1668 until his death in 1715, and part of the UNESCO-listed Champagne hillsides. Its slopes face south over the Marne and give ripe Pinot Noir and Meunier; it was rated 93% on the échelle.

Moët & Chandon owns the abbey, where Dom Pérignon is buried, and wrought-iron signs on the village houses show trades and wine scenes.

appellations.name: Moslins

appellations.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

appellations.name: Ambonnay
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, with some Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Ambonnay sits on the south-eastern flank of the Montagne de Reims, where the slope turns to face south and south-east over the Marne plain, next door to Bouzy. It is one of the great Pinot Noir villages of Champagne: its grapes are ripe, full and vinous, with a red-fruited depth that gives backbone to blends and makes Ambonnay a favourite for blanc de noirs and rosé. The village also makes still red Coteaux Champenois.

Krug's Clos d'Ambonnay, a walled plot of 0.68 ha first released with the 1995 vintage, is a pure Pinot Noir and one of the most expensive Champagnes made. Egly-Ouriet, whose long-aged, low-dosage wines are references for grower Champagne, Marguet (biodynamic), Paul Déthune and Eric Rodez are based here.
appellations.terroir: South and south-east-facing slopes of chalk under a thin cover of limestone scree and clay, at the foot of the forested Montagne plateau.
appellations.nerd_note: Krug's Clos d'Ambonnay is about a third of the size of its Clos du Mesnil, and the first vintage took 13 years to reach the market.
appellations.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

The village was the birthplace of Odo of Châtillon, Pope Urban II, who preached the First Crusade; a giant statue of him stands on the hill above the Marne.

appellations.name: Mareuil-sur-Aÿ
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A Pinot Noir premier cru along the Marne east of Aÿ, rated 99% on the old échelle, just short of grand cru, and since 2016 part of the commune of Aÿ-Champagne. It is the home of Billecart-Salmon and of Philipponnat, whose Clos des Goisses, a steep 5.5-ha walled slope facing south over the canal, is one of the most famous single vineyards in Champagne and is made in almost every year, a sign of how warm the site is.
appellations.nerd_note: 'Goisses' is said to come from an old local word for a very steep slope, and the Clos is one of the steepest vineyards in Champagne.
appellations.classification: Premier cru village: rated 99% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

appellations.terroir: Gentle, chalky land at the northern foot of the Montagne de Reims, on the edge of the city, where housing and roads have taken much of the old vineyard.
appellations.classification: Premier cru village: rated 94% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

appellations.name: Aÿ
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, with some Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Aÿ is the historic capital of Pinot Noir in Champagne and part of the UNESCO-listed Champagne Hillsides, Houses and Cellars (2015). Its steep, south-facing slopes above the Marne give powerful, ripe and vinous Pinot Noir that underpins the blends of the greatest houses. The wines of Aÿ were famous at the courts of France long before sparkling Champagne existed; Henri IV is said to have called himself 'Sire d'Aÿ'.

Bollinger, Deutz and Ayala are based here, and Henri Giraud and Gatinois are notable growers. Bollinger's Vieilles Vignes Françaises comes from small plots of ungrafted Pinot Noir in Aÿ, and its La Côte aux Enfants is a still red Coteaux Champenois. In April 1911 rioting growers burned houses in Aÿ suspected of using grapes from outside the region, which led to the delimitation of the Champagne zone. Since 2016 Aÿ forms the commune of Aÿ-Champagne with Mareuil-sur-Aÿ and Bisseuil.
appellations.terroir: Steep south-facing slopes above the Marne, chalk under limestone scree and marl.
appellations.nerd_note: Bollinger's ungrafted Vieilles Vignes Françaises vines survived phylloxera in walled plots and are trained en foule, the old layered planting method of Champagne.
appellations.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

appellations.name: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
The most austere and long-lived of the Chardonnay grand crus, on almost pure chalk at the southern end of the Côte des Blancs. Le Mesnil's wines are lean, piercing and saline when young and need years to show their depth; they are the reference for long-ageing blanc de blancs.

Salon, the original blanc de blancs, is made only from Le Mesnil grapes and only in exceptional years, and its sister house Delamotte is based here too. Krug's Clos du Mesnil, a walled vineyard of 1.85 ha first enclosed in 1698 and bought by Krug in 1971, gave its first vintage in 1979. Pierre Péters, Robert Moncuit, Guy Charlemagne, Pertois-Moriset and Jacques Selosse also make wines from it.
appellations.terroir: East-facing slopes of Belemnite chalk with very thin topsoil.
appellations.nerd_note: Pierre Péters' Les Chétillons, from three old parcels of Le Mesnil, is one of the most sought-after grower blanc de blancs.
appellations.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

appellations.name: Avize
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Avize is the heart of the Côte des Blancs, on the east-facing escarpment south of Cramant. Its Chardonnay is rich, saline and deep, with more body than Le Mesnil and more tension than Cramant, from chalk with a little more clay than its neighbours.

It is the home of the Lycée Viticole de la Champagne and of Anselme Selosse, who took over his father's vines in 1974 and changed Champagne by vinifying in barrels, farming for low yields and treating Champagne as a wine of place; his Substance is a solera begun in 1986. Agrapart, De Sousa and Varnier-Fannière are notable growers, and the Union Champagne cooperative (Champagne De Saint Gall) is based here. Big houses prize Avize fruit for blanc de blancs and prestige cuvées.
appellations.terroir: East-facing slopes of Belemnite chalk close to the surface, with a little more clay in the topsoil than in Le Mesnil.

appellations.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

appellations.summary: Romery is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 7 km north-west of Épernay. In the hills on the north side of the Marne, Meunier rules on clay-rich soils over deeper chalk, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; the wines are round and aromatic.

appellations.summary: Thil is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Massif de Saint-Thierry and the Vesle), about 8 km north-west of Reims. In the Saint-Thierry hills and along the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier leads on sands and clays over chalk, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on the chalkier slopes.

appellations.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Janvry is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Petite Montagne de Reims), about 11 km west of Reims. In the Petite Montagne de Reims west of the city, Meunier dominates on sandy and clay soils over chalk, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
appellations.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

appellations.name: Jouy-lès-Reims
appellations.grapes: Meunier, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A premier cru (90%) of the Petite Montagne de Reims, home of L. Aubry Fils, known for reviving the old Champagne varieties Arbane, Petit Meslier and Pinot Blanc alongside the main three.
appellations.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
appellations.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

appellations.name: Jaulgonne
appellations.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Jaulgonne is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 8 km west of Dormans, in the Aisne department. Meunier, which buds late and copes with the frost-prone valley, dominates the clay and marl slopes here; the base wines are round and fruit-forward, the softening element of many blends.

appellations.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
appellations.summary: La Neuville-aux-Larris is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 14 km north-west of Épernay. On the right bank of the Marne the main slopes face south toward the river; Meunier is the leading grape on clay and marl over chalk, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on the best sites.

appellations.name: Champillon
appellations.grapes: Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay
appellations.summary: A premier cru (93%) on the upper slopes above Dizy and Hautvillers, at the edge of the Montagne de Reims forest, with a famous view over the Marne valley to Épernay. Its south-facing vineyards give ripe but fresh fruit; the Royal Champagne hotel stands on the ridge above the vines.
appellations.terroir: Steep, south-facing slopes high on the Grande Vallée de la Marne, on chalk under marl and clay, with the forest above.
appellations.classification: Premier cru village: rated 93% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

appellations.name: Nanteuil-sur-Marne
appellations.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Nanteuil-sur-Marne is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 15 km south-west of Château-Thierry, in the Seine-et-Marne department. This is Meunier country: the chalk lies too deep to matter, and the clay-rich slopes along the valley give fleshy, early-maturing wines, many of them sold to the cooperatives of the Aisne.
